subject: Catalyst pilot — request for dedicated model affinity and warm-cache window
messages:
From: Sam Weber <sam.weber@catalyst.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <procurement@catalyst.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot details and a leaning ask on performance

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with latency and cost breakdowns. We're close to signing but a couple of technical asks came up in our internal architecture review that could materially affect our production timeline. High level: Catalyst needs predictable model affinity (we want the same model variant to stick to our tenant for the duration of the pilot) and a longer warm-cache window for KV/prefix caching so we don't see cold-start degradation during a long-running session workload.

Specifics:
- Affinity: our compliance folks prefer a per-tenant model binding for the pilot (no automatic fallback to other variants unless explicitly triggered).
- Warm-cache: requests are often bursty with gaps of 20–90 minutes; current cache expiry at our scale causes repeated re-warming and increased tail latency. We asked for a configurable warm-cache window up to 2 hours for the pilot.

We understand this touches runtime behavior. Before we go deep on SOW language, can your engineering/product team confirm feasibility and an estimated lift (engineering weeks)? We have internal deadlines to meet — if this can be scoped as a short-lived pilot feature with feature flags, we can close this quarter.

Attached a short one-pager on pilot traffic shape.

Best,
Sam
Director, Platform Engineering
Catalyst Systems
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sam Weber <sam.weber@catalyst.com>, Priya Rao <procurement@catalyst.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 11:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot details and a leaning ask on performance

Folks — forwarding Catalyst's asks. TL;DR: they need tenant-level model affinity + ability to extend warm-cache to ~2 hours for pilot to avoid repeated re-warms. This is a deal-closing ask; they indicated signing if we can treat this as a pilot flag and ship quickly.

Can you confirm estimated scope (engineering weeks), risk (SLO/regression areas), and whether we can gate behind a feature flag in Dedicated/Private? If we can’t do the exact affinity, what is the closest compatible behavior (e.g., routing policy pin by tenant id to a model-variant pool)?

I attached the SOW draft and their pilot traffic matrix. Happy to sync quickly — want to get an internal decision this week.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 09:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot details and a leaning ask on performance

Marissa / team,

Thanks for the context — high level thoughts after a quick review:

1) Tenant-level model affinity: technically feasible via routing policy + sticky assignment to a model-variant pool (we already have sticky affinity for session tokens). Implementing a per-tenant pin with explicit TTL is ~2–3 engineering weeks for the control-plane changes and rollout (can be behind a feature flag). Runtime changes are minor if we reuse existing affinity metadata. Risk: needs careful rollout to avoid capacity fragmentation across GPUs; we'll need an ops knob to rebalance.

2) Warm-cache window: increasing cache TTL for a tenant's KV/prefix cache to 2 hours is doable, but we need to quantify memory impact for Dedicated nodes. Implementation is likely 1–2 engineering weeks to add TTL config and an admin override. Risk: higher memory pressure and potential cross-tenant eviction behavior; we should test with a synthetic workload first.

3) Compatibility: If strict per-tenant model pinning is hard for Hosted customers, we can offer a Dedicated-only pilot mode that pins within a model-variant pool and provides warm-cache TTL. That path reduces risk and gives Catalyst the predictability they need.

I'll scope out a rough runbook and ask ops to provide an estimate of memory delta by Friday. Markus, can you weigh in on runtime/ops risk?

—Dev
Product Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Sam Weber <sam.weber@catalyst.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 13:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot details and a leaning ask on performance

Quick follow-up from infra/serving perspective:

We can implement tenant pinning as Dev described. Engineering estimate (end-to-end, including QA and a limited canary): 4 engineering weeks if we need an automation to rebalance pinned capacity, 2 weeks if Catalyst accepts manual ops rebalancing (short-term). Warm-cache TTL config is small work (1 week) but the real effort is in validation and load testing — I recommend we run a 48-hour soak in our staging cluster with the pilot traffic shape.

Operational considerations:
- We'll need explicit SLO language in the SOW: pinned tenants are best-effort for affinity; we cannot guarantee zero fallback unless Catalyst pays for dedicated capacity.
- Memory budgeting: for a 2-hour TTL at Catalyst's projected QPS, ops estimates an additional 10–15% memory usage on Dedicated nodes; this is acceptable but we must include an autoscale buffer.
- Rollout path: feature-flag → internal canary → customer pilot (Dedicated pool) → wider support.

If Sales wants commitment for a go/no-go timeline, propose: 3-week delivery if we accept manual ops runbook; 5 weeks for automated rebalancer and full QA. Both assume no major regressions during soak.

-Markus
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Weber <sam.weber@catalyst.com>, Priya Rao <procurement@catalyst.com>, Legal Team <legal@catalyst.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 10:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot details and a leaning ask on performance

Thanks — this is helpful and exactly what Catalyst needs to close. Sam/Priya: Redwood can offer the pilot on a Dedicated pool with the following commitments:

- Manual ops-backed tenant pinning + admin TTL adjustable to 2 hours for the warm-cache. Delivery in ~3 weeks (manual ops rebalancing).
- If Catalyst wants an automated rebalance and full QA with a longer guarantee window, we can do 5 weeks and add a small engineering uplift to cover automation work (we'll reflect in SOW).
- SOW will include operational caveat language: affinity best-effort; Dedicated pool reduces fallback risk; memory and autoscale buffer details included.

If you can confirm preference (manual ops vs automated) and sign the SOW draft, we can lock timelines and schedule the staging soak. Priya — can you share vendor PO timeline?

Next steps for Redwood internal team: Dev — please prepare a short runbook and canary checklist; Markus — coordinate ops for memory budget and soak plan; Hannah — I'll need a customer success playbook (communication plan during the soak).

Sam — appreciate the fast feedback. If we get confirmation today, I'll circulate an updated SOW and a proposed start date.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
